note: One record per control class. sees and blind_spot are the pair that matters: a control is only as good as what it structurally cannot observe.

classes.name: object level authorisation
classes.mechanism: a per object ownership check on every read and write, evaluated after the object is fetched
classes.sees: the caller and the record owner, when both are present at the same layer
classes.blind_spot: paths that fetch the object without going through the checked function, such as a bulk export, a report, a relation traversal or an admin view
classes.bypass: reach the object through any route that does not call the checked function
classes.cost: low: usually a parameter change on an alternate endpoint
classes.detection: an access log where one principal touches objects whose owner column differs, correlated across endpoints

classes.name: function level authorisation
classes.mechanism: a role or permission check per operation, deny by default, declared centrally
classes.sees: the operation name and the caller's role set
classes.blind_spot: operations that are composed at runtime, and the difference between a role that exists and a role that should reach this object
classes.bypass: find an operation not covered by the declaration, or one whose declaration is stale
classes.cost: low to medium: needs route enumeration, rewarded by any undocumented endpoint
classes.detection: a request to a route with no matching policy entry, which is a configuration alert rather than a traffic one

classes.name: binding allowlist
classes.mechanism: an explicit field allowlist per operation, never object hydration from request data
classes.sees: the field names the request carries
classes.blind_spot: nested and association writes, where the allowlist covers the parent and the child object is bound by a different rule
classes.bypass: write through a relation or a batch operation the allowlist does not model
classes.cost: low if a relation exists, medium otherwise
classes.detection: a write where a field changed that the endpoint's allowlist does not contain

classes.name: identity canonicalisation
classes.mechanism: one normalisation form for every identifier, exact match, verified linking between providers
classes.sees: the identifier as submitted and its canonical form
classes.blind_spot: identifiers the canonicaliser does not know about, such as provider specific aliases, unicode confusables and case folding that differs per backend
classes.bypass: find two spellings that pass canonicalisation and collide at the store
classes.cost: medium: requires probing the normaliser, not guessing it
classes.detection: two accounts or sessions resolving from one credential, visible as a uniqueness violation after the fact

classes.name: state machine integrity
classes.mechanism: invariants enforced per transition, with separation of duties where the process requires it
classes.sees: the current state and the requested transition
classes.blind_spot: the same invariant expressed in two places, such as an API and a batch job, and any transition performed by a migration
classes.bypass: act on the state directly through a second writer
classes.cost: medium: needs a second surface that writes the same record
classes.detection: a state value reached without the transition event that should precede it

classes.name: credential and token policy
classes.mechanism: atomic single use for reset and invite tokens, subset scopes for delegation, verified identity for every claim
classes.sees: the token's claims, signature, expiry and use count
classes.blind_spot: the lifetime of the permission behind the token, and every token minted before a revocation
classes.bypass: use a token inside its validity window after the permission behind it changed
classes.cost: low if a revocation window exists, high otherwise
classes.detection: a token used after the subject's rights changed, correlated on subject rather than on token

classes.name: parser strictness
classes.mechanism: one parser for the whole path, rejecting duplicates, alternates and ambiguous framing
classes.sees: the bytes it parsed and anything it rejected
classes.blind_spot: the other parser downstream, whose existence is the entire precondition for a desync
classes.bypass: find a second interpreter in the path and a message both accept differently
classes.cost: medium: needs a byte level client and knowledge of the chain
classes.detection: a request the edge logged differently from the origin, which requires comparing two logs rather than one

classes.name: path and namespace control
classes.mechanism: canonicalise once, then verify containment against a fixed root, with no user controlled path component
classes.sees: the canonical path and whether it sits under the root
classes.blind_spot: symlinks and junctions created after the check, and any component the application resolves later
classes.bypass: create a link between check and use, or reach a resolver that reinterprets the name
classes.cost: medium to high: needs a write primitive as well as a read
classes.detection: a resolved path whose realpath differs from the checked path, which almost nobody logs

classes.name: cache and key discipline
classes.mechanism: every input that varies the response is part of the key, and authenticated responses never enter a shared cache
classes.sees: the key it built and the response it stored
classes.blind_spot: inputs it did not model, such as a header it forwards, a cookie it ignores and normalisation it applies after keying
classes.bypass: find an input that changes the response and is absent from the key
classes.cost: low: usually one request to plant, one to read
classes.detection: a cached response whose body contains a value from a different request's headers, found by diffing stored objects

classes.name: cost and resource control
classes.mechanism: per operation cost budgets and per principal quotas, enforced before the work is done
classes.sees: the declared cost of an operation and the principal's spend so far
classes.blind_spot: operations whose real cost differs from the declared one, which is every resolver that expands a relation
classes.bypass: find an operation that under declares its cost
classes.detection: spend per operation diverging from the declared budget across a population of requests

classes.name: audit integrity
classes.mechanism: structured append only logging with attribution, held where the audited identity cannot edit it
classes.sees: the acts the application chose to log, and the principal the application believed
classes.blind_spot: acts performed through a path that does not log, and any act where the principal was fabricated upstream
classes.bypass: act through an unlogged path, or make the log attribute the act to someone else
classes.cost: low if an unlogged path exists
classes.detection: a state change with no corresponding audit record, found by reconciling state against the log rather than reading the log

classes.name: protocol lifecycle
classes.mechanism: retired versions decommissioned, one policy point rather than one per version
classes.sees: the version in use and whether it is still permitted
classes.blind_spot: the older version nobody decommissioned, and the policy point that only some routes pass through
classes.bypass: use a version or a route that skips the policy point
classes.detection: traffic on a version whose retirement date has passed, which is a configuration report

classes.name: maintenance and process
classes.mechanism: controls that live in process, infrastructure or review: patching cadence, dependency freshness, offboarding, review depth
classes.sees: whether a step in the process happened, if anyone records it
classes.blind_spot: the gap between the process and the work, and every exception granted under time pressure
classes.bypass: wait for the gap, or find the exception that was never revoked
classes.cost: time rather than requests, which is why it is the cheapest class for a patient attacker
classes.detection: a step that has no record, and a control whose exception register has no expiry

classes.name: unclassified
classes.mechanism: no mechanism: the counter did not match any class, which is a classifier gap rather than a control
classes.sees: nothing, because it is an absence
classes.blind_spot: whatever the unmatched counters were describing
classes.bypass: not applicable; an unclassified counter means the taxonomy needs the case, not that a bypass exists
classes.detection: the size of this class itself, which should stay small and does not always
